utterances.text: Doctor, sorry, I did not properly ask the question. There is something in brackets. It says, "1st of January to 1st of June," and that is what you just told us. So this document does not purport to claim that all these persons, from 1 to 76, were employed there throughout this period? This is not what we can conclude from this list, but that for a period of time, for a segment of time within this time frame, they did work, so perhaps only in January or only in some other month, but they did for a while, did they work here? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, this is not really correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But didn't the majority of these people come as full-time employees?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could tick off those who did work during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you do that? Great.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but I have no pencil or anything to do that, and I need some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How is this going to help us, first of all?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Because some persons are later either mentioned or connected to various different incidents. Like, for example, one of the doctors mentioned under 74, I'm just about to introduce one document and ask whether that could be his document, knowing that he was there at the time. Perhaps if I put a little bit simpler question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you please say that there are some persons who never came for work during that period of time, who never came for work during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Listen, this is from the 1st of January. I can tell you who did not report for work as of the 16th of April, '93, because we all worked until the 16th of April, '93, in the health centre in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the institution of the health centre, regardless of its moving to another location, it was the same institution, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So my question is, it transpires from this document that -- at least that's how I see it -- that these people, these 76 individuals, worked for the health centre at least one day, at least one day within this time frame between the 1st of January and the 1st of June. I know that it changed.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Please, they were all there until the 16th of April, with the exception of Gordan Pehar, they all worked there until the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I see. All right. Okay, fine, thank you. So until the 16th of April --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Except Gordan Pehar, who was not a full-time employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Then, Your Lordships, with your leave, I will adduce this document-- of course, when we make the translation. I mean, I should like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. When it's translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Doctor, yesterday you told us that two HVO members, and you even gave us their names, Ratko Nuk and Kovac, nicknamed Zabac --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Anto Kovac, nicknamed Zabac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- took you to the building housing the HVO command? And I'm referring to the 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, in the evening, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You also said that you realised then that it was -- that the office that took you in was the office of my client, Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, in that office I found Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right, but was it his office?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the house of the cultural, the cultural centre, so he presumably moved in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the office, the office in which you saw Mario Cerkez, are you positive that it was his office, or just one of the offices in that building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I saw him in one of the offices in that a building. That is where I saw -- where I met Mario Cerkez. But I never saw Mario Cerkez in that particular office. I never before came to that office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. So you saw him in one of the offices, but you do not know who this office belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that was the property of the cultural centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Was there an inscription on the door of that office? Did you have an opportunity to look at it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not pay any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. According to what you told us, according to a your testimony, and you repeated it several times, Mario Cerkez gave you the exact number of prisoners, 2.223.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And because the figure was so exact, you remembered it, isn't it? It just stuck in your memory, it was so characteristic? In your earlier statement to investigators on the 1st of March, '95, you said -- and I shall give you that statement, if you would like your memory to be jogged -- that Santic and Skopljak, when you talked to them, said 2.323?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I should like to tender the earlier statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I wonder how much we're going to be helped. It's a difference in one figure, is it, out of the four? You've put it to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I can agree with the figure, even it's a little bit different, but the other persons. Could I ask the usher to distribute ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D15/2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Kovacic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Sorry. I just explained that on the top there is an English version and on the bottom is Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian language, of the document. (No interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Doctor, would you please be kind enough to look at the first page to see which statement we are referring to? So it is your statement made to the investigators of this Tribunal. Do we see it is the 1st of March, 1995? Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know that I made statements in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to look at page 3 in the Croatian text. In the English version it is page 5, or M0099. (No interpretation) In the middle of that paragraph. (Interpretation) Doctor, I wish to draw your attention to this sentence, beginning at 05.00: "Ivica Santic and Pero Skopljak came and threatened us that if the BH army attack us, they will kill all the people in the basement plus 2.323 prisoners throughout Vitez." Is your statement noted correctly?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me tell you that I complained several times on the very poor translations. I said "2223," and I did not at all say it in this way. The figure was mentioned to me by Mario Cerkez. Ivica Santic and Pero Skopljak never mentioned any figures. So this is a poor translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Doctor, do you think that it is possible to make errors when translating names? Do you think that is possible? It's only names that are wrong, possibly, and a figure, a number?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I'm repeating what I said in the Prosecutor's office. I drew attention several times to the fact that the translation was poor, and I did so yesterday as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right, then, so you attribute the difference to the translation, errors in the translation?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I never said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Tell us, Doctor, when you started your conversation with Cerkez, you said that he was in the office together with some others. What exactly did Cerkez ask you to do?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yesterday, I said what Cerkez asked. He said, "Doctor, are you aware of the position you are in?" Had I heard about Ahmici? I answered in the affirmative. After that, he said that I must do as he bids me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what did he ask you to do?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First he said, "Doctor, do you know where Dubravica and Zabrdze are?" That is where the BH army has broken through the lines and is entering Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, we heard about that. But what did he ask you to actually do?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said yesterday that Mr. Cerkez said to me that I must call up the command of the 3rd Corps and the Bosnian politicians and tell them that there were 2.223 prisoners in Vitez, and if they continued their advance, they would issue orders for the prisoners to be killed. Secondly, what he said to me after that was after this conversation on the phone, that I must go on television and call on the Muslims of Stari Vitez to surrender their weapons, and the third point he made was that he asked me to select the members of a commission to negotiate with the HVO. Together with Zvonko Cilic he sent me to the basement and said that there were about 300 prisoners there and that I could choose whoever I wanted for those negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Okay. So those were those three requests he made of you. With Their Honours' permission, I should like to tender this exhibit, which we have in translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I tender this document, translated into Croatian and French, the same document having been admitted in the Blaskic case, as D316. Could the usher help me distribute it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Again, at the top is the Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, and then come the English and the French translations.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D16/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mujezinovic, would you be kind enough to read this document. The 18th of April, 1993, just for yourself. You don't have to read it out loud. Doctor, had you heard about the negotiations that are mentioned here in the preamble to the order between Mate Boban and Alija Izetbegovic held on the 18th of April, 1993, in Zagreb, and the agreement reached at those talks?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is a day prior to the event we had just discussed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I hadn't heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But did you hear about it later?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell us that you never heard about talks between Mate Boban and Ilija Izetbegovic held on the 18th of April in Zagreb which produced a certain agreement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot be specific. I know that there were many negotiations and talks, but I do not recall this particular date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me something else, then, so this is a document of the 18th of April, and according to your statement, on the 19th of April, Cerkez forced you to take certain steps to halt the attack on Vitez, and attack by the BH army. Why, when he already had in his hands an order referring to a cease-fire that had been reached, what could possibly be the motives?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told you literally what Cerkez said to me. As for his motives, I'm not familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Doctor, regards his second request to appear on television, did you fulfil that request?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, after going to the basement, I selected a certain number of people. Zvonko Cilic went with me, with the military police, and I and Zvonko Cilic -- actually Zvonko Cilic helped me, to draft a text which was very awkward for me, the one that was proposed, and then I spoke on local Croatian television at 1.00 a.m. And this statement was aired for two or three days repeatedly, that is, my statement, what I had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zvonko Cilic was your friend, one might say?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zvonko Cilic was my associate at work. He was a social worker, and he worked in the commission for prevention, of which I was the chairman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You were on good terms with him?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We were both members of the football club in Vitez. We collaborated well. I would frequently go to examine his mother, and we were on good terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the drafting of the text, was it imposed upon you or did he assist you in the wording?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He agreed with the text that I was going to read on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it. Did Zvonko or anyone else produce a text and give it to you and say, "This is what you have to read"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Zvonko agreed to what I had proposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As a man who engaged in journalism, he agreed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I took down what I was going to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I should like to show the Court the statement made by the witness, taken off the Vitez Television. It only lasts one minute. I have given the interpreters the transcript in B/C/S, so could they translate it for us? (In English) Thank you. (Interpretation) Could the technical booth please find tape number 3, and the very beginning of that tape? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (Voiceover) "I have been told that it was announced in the media that I had been killed, arrested. I can tell you that that is not true. I'm now in the emergency ward of the health clinic, that I am working as a doctor, specialist, and that I'm extending aid to all those who come to the emergency ward of the health clinic."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is just a part of what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it's not your complete statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is there more that comes before or after? You don't know?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you did say this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In fact, I think that this recording has nothing -- is not linked to it. This is a statement that I gave at 1.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood you. Is this part of the statement that you made?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is just a part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But it is a part of that statement that was broadcast that night?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a part of it, but it is not complete. But the main part of it was not shown, was not viewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Kovacic, I'm sorry, from the Chamber's point of view, we have a problem here. You're giving a part of that statement, of that broadcast on video. We don't have the text. Could we not have the text, perhaps, a transcript of the whole of the broadcast, because we cannot take an excerpt without having the context of the statement? This is a problem for us, a problem of appreciation of what it intends to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, I asked Vitez Television to give me the statement that I had learned during the investigation had been broadcast. I received this, and this is the first that I hear that this is only a part of that statement. All I can do is try again, but unfortunately I didn't have time to check because I had very little time for the preparations, as you know. All I can do is ask Vitez Television to look through their archives and to find the rest, possibly. This is the first time I hear that this is just a part of it. That's why I asked the witness whether this was the beginning, the end, or the middle.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "This is just a part of the statement," said the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One way of dealing with the matter may be to ask the witness whether he can remember anything else he said. Meanwhile, if you return to the television studio to see whether there is anything you could get from them. I mean, I don't mean you personally, I mean that some enquires are made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I certainly will, and I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Doctor, you have heard the debate. You said it was just a part of that statement. Could you perhaps tell us, do you remember did this come at the beginning and then comes the rest, or is it the end, or is it the middle of the statement, if you can remember? If not, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this is the end of my statement. I can tell Their Honours -- I can repeat to Their Honours here, as they had just suggested, that I tell them what I actually said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do. Please do tell us what is missing.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said as following: That I called on all the Croats and all the Muslims not to shoot at each other, because this was of no benefit to either people, that it benefited only the Karadzic's Chetniks. And I appealed on all to cease conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So that is, in fact, what you said in your statement to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Kovacic, could the witness tell us whether this statement was a statement he made freely, of his own free will?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was ordered to make a statement. I was ordered to make a different statement in a different version, but what I actually said was what I have just told you, and I would have said the same thing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you are saying that you were ordered the content of this statement you were supposed to make, but what you actually said did not correspond to that order, so you said something that you would have said anyway?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Zvonko helped me. And I said I could say this, and he did not oppose my saying this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you because you did not obey?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Doctor, tell me, please, why the health centre was moved from its original location to a reserve location for those couple of days between the 16th and the 18th, until you came to work.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The 16th of what, when?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You said April '93, when the conflict started, you said that you stayed at home, and you came to work for the first time on the 19th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The health centre, when you returned to work on the 19th, was it in this reserve location in the craft centre?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear the reason for the move?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So from the 20th of October, when it was moved, it stayed there in the reserve location?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. When was the health centre moved from its original location to its reserve location in the craft centre?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We used that location in October. I said that a part had been moved then. Then we returned because the health centre had not been damaged at the time. I said I came to work on the 19th at the reserve location of the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So please be brief. The centre was moved to its reserve location for preventative reasons for the first time in connection with the conflict of the 20th of October, 1992, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It was moved for a second time without your knowledge, when you were not present, between the 16th and the 19th of April, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it was moved, but I said between, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were you at work until the beginning of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was, on the 15th of April, at my workplace in the health centre in Vitez, at the original location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And when you returned to work on the 19th or, rather, when you were brought to work, it had already moved to its reserve location. Therefore, it is clear that it was moved sometime between the 15th and the 19th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I found that it had been moved. When exactly it was moved, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did the staff tell you why it had been moved to the reserve location?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Could Your Honours allow me to show a very brief video clip without any text? For the technical booth, tape number 1, the scene at the very beginning of the tape. There is a marking of the time. It says, "7.53 hours on the 16th of April, 1993." There is no text. We will just see a scene which I think is self-explanatory. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) We can stop there, technical booth, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, there were, in fact, voices on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Entirely irrelevant. I was trying to pick up -- those were background voices of the persons who were in the same room from which some of the shots were taken. I don't think there is any value, and I did my best to recognise at least a word or two. Entirely useless. There even seems there was a British officer in the office. I caught once or twice the English words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What do you want to ask about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very simple, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Are these shots of the centre of the town of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a very poor film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you see any recognisable sites like the department store, the post office building? Can you confirm that this is downtown Vitez, between the post office, the Workers' Centre, the central [indiscernible], the department store, between the cultural centre and the SDK or the old pharmacy? So would you confirm it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it is, but I think the film is very poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The health centre, where was it originally located? It was not far from here, was it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: About 150 metres away, maybe less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As many metres as you said from this square that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "From this park," said the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you see a shell hit the municipality building towards the end?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't. We saw about 12 people injured by a shell. Among them was an Englishman who was waging war on the HVO side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Mujezinovic, was whether you heard or saw, from your window, shells falling on the centre of Vitez in the days you didn't go to work?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I really don't know. A war is a war. I didn't ask many questions. I was working. I tried to tell you that while I was working, a shell hit the post office and that we had 10 or 12 injured people, among whom was an Englishman. But whether there were shells before that, I really couldn't say. I know that Dr. Franjo Tibold told me that there were many dead, but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I understand that. But tell me, please, when you came to work on the 19th, didn't you ask why the health centre had been moved to a reserve location which was far less favourable than in the original?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite correct, but we were safer here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Safer from what?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Shells or anything, because I had chosen that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So there was shelling of the town?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that. I didn't go into town. I was working. I said I was driven to and from work and my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you never saw a single -- or heard a single shell fall nearby?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do know that there was shelling and I heard shells, but I personally didn't see them, nor the extent of the damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go back to the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you want to continue or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's try and finish at least your cross-examination, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: My guess is I will need about half an hour, so for tomorrow morning, perhaps 15 minutes, 20 minutes. (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Tomorrow morning. Mr. Kovacic, I must ask you to complete your cross-examination in half an hour tomorrow, if you would set your mind to it. Mr. Sayers, I hope you're not going to be too long, since Mr. Kovacic has borne the brunt of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Kovacic has been extremely thorough, and I would hope, Your Honour, to be less than half an hour myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could I just raise the question of remaining witnesses for the week, if the Court is about to adjourn?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: (redacted) is here, and his material is being prepared. In case it's going to help the Court, we just had this document. I trust a similar document will be available for a volume of material that is much smaller in quantity. I think it's about that much to read, and that includes the B/C/S translations. It deals with another municipality, so that in theory, it could take quite a long time, because municipalities, in theory and according to the plan I've made, have to be dealt with thoroughly. But were you to read the material, you would probably think it was very familiar and very similar to what you've heard before. It's not, of course, the same. It's simply that things unfolded in the different municipalities in a similar way. So we have it in mind, as a possibility, that we can deal with this witness shortly, if that's acceptable to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stein?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I rise because I don't know what document Mr. Nice is referring to, and we haven't been supplied with same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us release the doctor. Dr. Mujezinovic, I'm afraid you've got to come back tomorrow, but it will be the last day. If you would like to go now, rather than wait for this, could you be back, please, at 9.45? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED MUJEZINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, which municipality are we going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Indiscernible], which you can find -- if any of you is using this map, which you can find to the south of Busovaca, over the fold, and then down there. It's not itemised as a municipality, the subject of a tax or anything of that sort. It's included for the Prosecution Count 1. The document that I was referring to and that Mr. Stein doesn't have is a document that I don't have yet. It's a document that Mr. Scott, who is preparing this witness, is, I hope, preparing at the moment, and it will be another route map, through the limited number of statements that this witness has made, identifying the topics that he can deal with. The reason I'm interested to know whether we can deal with him swiftly is because, of course, if we can deal with him shortly and properly, then I will ensure that Mr. McLeod flies across tomorrow in order that we can use Thursday and Friday morning with him. I realise that again will impose something of a burden on the Chamber, because it would suggest that McLeod's report could be preread, but there's a balancing exercise here between getting the evidence in properly, swiftly, and being completely free from reading outside court. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which are the documents you want us to read?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the Court is prepared, in the case of (redacted), to have and to consider reading his witness statements, our guess is it would take, perhaps, experienced judges 30 minutes to read, and that would probably be about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We certainly would be prepared to do that. Yes, Mr. Stein?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: This raises the issue we're going to be addressing tomorrow and a theme throughout this case, and the Prosecution's continuing invitation for Your Honours to read the witness statements for their tactical judgements that that will impress on you, because you will see it first-hand with your own eyes and read it in your own way is the importance of the statements. We oppose that. We've always opposed it and continue to oppose it. In fact, as I will state clearly today and tomorrow, the reading of the documents will guarantee -- the reading of the statements in the fashion that the Prosecutor suggests will guarantee that the cross-examination will be more prolonged than less, whereas I intend to propose something tomorrow that I think can resolve the issue I've just raised and the Prosecutor's concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Stein, I don't think this prejudges, in any way, what we're going to discuss in the afternoon or the decisions to be taken by the Chamber. As you know with Judge May, he converted us to his culture of working in a pragmatic way, so we avoid general rules and we're working in a practical way, in a pragmatic way. So this is a very concrete and practical proposal that is being made to us, and we would like you to accept it, and then we'll see about more general stuff. But for the time being, I think we should be practical, if we want to get ahead with this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Very good, Your Honour, and actually I'll be proposing some, I like to think, practical ways and modern advocacy tomorrow afternoon as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we'll consider that. But as far as this witness is concerned, if we can have copies of the statements, we'll read them. What we read in the statements, may I emphasise, is not the evidence. It is the evidence which is given which counts. But I hope that this will speed things up. So there's no need to cross-examine what's in the statements, unless you want to controvert something as a result of it. We are not a jury. I make that point yet again. We are not a jury. We are quite capable of distinguishing between what is evidence and what merely appears in a statement, and putting out of our minds entirely something which is in a statement. But if it's going to assist us to get on with it, so much the better. The only thing is we don't have a copy of the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, as the Court will remember, Ms. Featherstone has a master copy in her room. I'll make arrangements with her to ensure that either we or she copies the statements and that all of the statements are in English. I'm afraid they are not yet in French. There is an exercise under way, Judge Bennouna, to have all the statements translated to French, both for yourself and, indeed, for Mr. Lopez-Terres, who would prefer them in French, and they will be with you, in your offices, I hope within half an hour, at the very maximum, or shorter if that's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, I apologise for asking for the floor, but I wish to make just one point. Of course, I understand that you have every right to read these statements and will do so, but as for the witness that is coming tomorrow, one of the statements is a statement which, according to our law, cannot be considered as evidence in court, and I should like you to bear that fact in mind. Namely, it is a statement given to a body which, according to the law of the former Yugoslavia, including the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, had no authority to take a statement which would automatically be used as evidence in court, nor was the citizen warned of the necessity to speak the truth and all the other notices that are given to a witness normally when making a statement. And this is just something I wish to draw Your Honour's attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which statement is that, and to what body?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) It's one of the statements outside the statement taken by the investigator. I can look it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think, Mr. Naumovski, that's sufficient to identify it. That is sufficient to identify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) It's a statement dated the 5th of June, 1997, which that witness gave to AID, the agency for research and documentation in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll bear that in mind when we look at the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If we can have the statements as soon as possible, we'll read them, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Scott's document is available. I'll distribute that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would, please. And we'll meet again at 9.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
